title: SDK-side telemetry backpressure and prioritized span emission
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Problem: SDKs that emit tracing and lightweight telemetry for streaming LLM requests are contributing measurable CPU/IO overhead and amplifying tail latency under high client concurrency. Current approach emits spans/metrics synchronously or with naive unbounded buffers which leads to client-side stalls and dropped telemetry during backpressure. Goal: implement a client-side emission protocol that applies adaptive batching, prioritized span tagging, and backpressure-aware flush policies to keep SDK overhead low while preserving fidelity for latency/error analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Client SDK emits at most 1 TCP write per 50ms per connection under steady-state traffic while preserving end-to-end traceability for critical spans
Sampling hints (high/medium/low) attached to spans result in >=95% of high-priority spans being delivered under load
No increase >3% in p95 latency for streaming generate API observed in Canary customers when SDK with coalescer is enabled
Automated e2e test validates graceful degradation under simulated network stalls and verifies eventual delivery/retry semantics
implementation_plan: Design telemetry gate component in SDK that holds small in-memory micro-batches (configurable max_bytes, max_spans, max_age_ms)
Add span urgency field with value set by server hints or SDK heuristics (error, user-interaction, model-call-start/end)
Implement priority-driven flush: flush immediately for 'error' urgency, coalesce for 'normal', defer for 'background' until batch thresholds or timer expires

Backpressure handling: when downstream emit channel signals saturated, throttle spans but preserve high-urgency items; implement exponential backoff and persistent queue to disk (rotating file) capped by size
Introduce lightweight handshake with ingestion endpoint to signal transient acceptance window and enable adaptive batch sizing per-client-region
Integrate sampling hint propagation to server-side collectors so backend can correlate and avoid further sampling of already low-urgency spans
Add feature flag and runtime config via Console to toggle coalescer and tuning knobs per-customer
Add unit and integration tests + chaos tests that simulate packet loss and slow consumers
Rollout: internal dogfood -> small Canary customer group (5 customers) -> opt-in beta -> default on for SDK minor release
design_notes: Avoid changing the public span schema: add 'urgency' as well-known optional attribute so existing processors ignore if absent
Prefer passive disk queue rather than synchronous DB for edge SDKs to keep dependency surface minimal
We debated protobuf vs JSON for transport; protobuf chosen for compactness, but shim supports JSON fallback for legacy endpoints
Retention guarantees: SDK will attempt delivery for up to 2 hours (configurable) then drop oldest low-priority entries
Security: on-disk queue is encrypted using OS-level storage encryption; ensure no PII is written by default
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: disk queue could grow on devices with limited storage. Mitigation: strict size cap and early eviction policy based on urgency.
Risk: changing batching semantics could alter observed timing in dashboards. Mitigation: annotate emitted spans with 'emit_delay_ms' and run side-by-side comparison in Canary to calibrate dashboards.
Risk: handshake increases server-side state. Mitigation: design handshake as ephemeral token with soft limits and avoid per-connection persistent state in the ingestion tier.

Risk: clients behind NAT may open few connections; coalescing must avoid head-of-line blocking. Mitigation: allow per-request immediate flush for high-urgency spans and small max_age_ms values for streaming APIs.
observability_goals: Expose SDK emit metrics: records_emitted_total, records_dropped_total, current_queue_size, avg_emit_latency_ms
Add dashboard tile in Console for SDK health with global heatmap of dropped telemetry by region
Instrument server ingestion to surface mismatch between urgency label and backend sampling decisions
Create alert: dropped_high_urgency_spans_rate > 0.1% for 5m triggers P1 pager
testing_plan: Unit tests for micro-batcher boundaries and priority flush rules
Integration tests with local ingestion service simulating backpressure and slow consumers
Chaos test: randomized network loss and disk full scenarios run in CI nightly
Canary behavioral test comparing p95 latency and telemetry completeness between old-sdk and new-sdk cohorts
rollout_strategy: Feature-flag gated in SDK release (minor) with default OFF
Enable for internal services and CI runners for 1 week; monitor SDK metrics
Enable for 5 small Canary customers with manual opt-in; run two-week observation
Gradual ramp to 50% of new signups; after success enable-by-default and backfill documentation
notes: Dashboard prototype: Console -> Observability -> SDK Telemetry -> Emit Health (temporary)
Related infra work: ingestion admission control sprint (ENG-431210) must land before handshake is enabled
